expectations.text: Output sides with the advisor — OLS with two-way fixed effects and firm-level cluster-robust SEs is a defensible, standard approach for linear panel data with 800 clusters
expectations.evidence: "Your advisor is right. Reviewer #2 is wrong" — the response unambiguously endorses TWFE with clustered SEs as "the gold-standard identification strategy in empirical economics for exactly this data structure."

expectations.text: Output does NOT agree with Reviewer #2 that the approach is 'invalid' or requires MLM to be publishable
expectations.evidence: "Why Reviewer #2's objection is mistaken" section explicitly rejects the invalid framing; MLM is recommended only as a robustness check, not a requirement: "run a multilevel model as a robustness check only."

expectations.text: Output explains that firm fixed effects already absorb all time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity at the firm level — which is the main thing MLM random effects add; stacking MLM random effects on top of FEs is unusual and doesn't add identification value in a linear model
expectations.evidence: "FE *absorbs* it, which is stronger than modeling it" and "Fixed effects are strictly more robust than the random effects in a multilevel model." The response conveys that FE subsumes what RE adds, making MLM redundant or inferior in this setting.

expectations.text: Output explains that with 800 clusters and a linear outcome, cluster-robust SEs are reliable and OLS+CRSE is the standard panel econometrics approach for this design
expectations.evidence: "800 clusters is well above any threshold for asymptotic validity (rule of thumb: ≥ 30–50)" and citing Cameron & Miller (2015) on cluster-robust inference directly addresses both the reliability of CRSE and its disciplinary standard status.

expectations.text: Output correctly notes when MLM would add genuine value over CRSE: fewer clusters (<30), interest in cross-level interactions or variance components, or needing predictions for new out-of-sample clusters
expectations.evidence: The response never identifies the conditions under which MLM would genuinely outperform CRSE. It mentions "shrinkage matters more for 1–2 obs/group" (which confuses within-unit observations with cluster count) but never discusses few clusters (<30), cross-level interactions, variance components estimation, or out-of-sample cluster prediction as legitimate MLM use cases.
